subject: Post-demo: recommended model shortlist & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Subject: Post-demo: recommended model shortlist & next steps

Thanks again for taking the demo today — great discussion. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment:

What I heard:
- You need real-time summarization and guided Q&A over customer support tickets (90% of volume), with strict 250ms tail-latency targets for the web UI.
- Budget sensitivity: procurement is aiming for a predictable per-1k-token cost that is below your current managed provider spend by ~25%.
- Quality bar: human-rated accuracy for summaries should be >= 90% on our shared eval prompts; low tolerance for hallucinations on policy questions.

Immediate recommended next steps:
1) I put together a short model shortlist + tradeoffs (latency / cost / quality) and a small prompt set for your team to run locally on a quick eval. See attached report + prompt set.
2) If the shortlist looks OK, we can run a 72-hour canary on your dedicated pool (we’ll surface token cost estimates and perf metrics).
3) Rishi (cc’d) will follow up on a preliminary pricing estimate and any procurement questions.

Attachments: redwood_acme_eval_report_v1.pdf (summary + benchmarks), prompt_set_acme.zip (20 canonical prompts + human eval rubric), latency_cost_matrix.csv (approx unit economics).

Ask: Please confirm who on your side should receive the evaluation notebook (we can share via Drive or S3) and whether legal needs an NDA before we share the raw signal files.

Thanks,

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Post-demo: recommended model shortlist & next steps

Jordan — great questions. High level answers and the shortlist below. Full details in the attached PDF and the Drive notebook link.

Shortlist (recommended order) with rationale:

1) LlamaX-7B-fp4 (Redwood-optimized) — Best balance for your use case\- Quality: ~91–93% on our support-summary eval suite (meets your >=90% bar)\- Latency: estimated P95 ~180–220ms on a 1x A10 dedicated instance with Redwood continuous batching and KV cache enabled\- Cost: lowest per-token cost of the high-quality options due to quantized fp4 path\- Notes: strong for extractive/abstractive summaries; watch for edge-case hallucinations on policy language (we include a focused prompt guardrail set)
\2) Falcon-40B-instruct (quantized) — Higher quality + higher cost\- Quality: ~94–96% on our evals (best on nuanced policy Qs)\- Latency: P95 ~320–380ms on similar hardware (likely exceeds your 250ms target unless we use a larger fleet or lower concurrency)\- Cost: ~2.5x LlamaX-7B-fp4 per-token; recommended only if your product prioritizes quality over strict latency
\3) Mix-and-fallback (LlamaX-7B primary + Falcon-40B for policy-critical prompts)\- Rationale: keep LlamaX for most traffic; route policy-sensitive queries to Falcon for higher accuracy. This yields approx +15–25% cost overhead vs. pure LlamaX but can reduce critical hallucination incidents.
\Benchmarks / assumptions summary:
- All latency estimates assume Redwood dedicated pool with our continuous-batching runtime and 200ms extra network overhead budget (P95).
- Cost estimates use 72-hour steady-state throughput assumptions (prompt length 120 tokens, response 60 tokens). See latency_cost_matrix.csv for the full matrix.
\Next recommended steps:
- If you want to validate quickly: we can provision a 72-hour canary for LlamaX-7B-fp4 and run your prompt set. We’ll return per-prompt quality scores and P95 latency distribution.
- If you want stricter latency guarantees, we can propose a capacity plan (reserved instances) and a fall-back routing policy for policy questions.
\Drive link to eval notebook: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b3c-redwood-acme-evals (view-only).
\I’ll ask Rishi to send a preliminary back-of-envelope pricing for the two scenarios (pure LlamaX vs mix-and-fallback).
\Thanks,
Marissa

Quick pricing + procurement note (preliminary) — sharing ballpark to help your procurement planning:

Scenario A — LlamaX-7B-fp4 (72h canary, dedicated pool)\- Expected token throughput: 1.2M tokens/day\- Estimated unit cost: $0.45 per 1k tokens\- Estimated 72h cost: $1160 (includes infra overhead + Redwood serving runtime)
\Scenario B — Mix-and-fallback (LlamaX primary + Falcon-40B for policy traffic ~10% of queries)\- Estimated unit cost blended: $0.75 per 1k tokens\- Estimated 72h cost: $1920
\Notes and next steps:
- These are preliminary estimates; I can convert to a month-to-month committed reserved plan if you prefer a lower effective unit price.
- We’ll need a short procurement form (I’ll send a one-page SOW template) and an Ops contact to provision the dedicated pool. Priya — who should I coordinate with for provisioning?
